findings.why: 'she took herself off his lips' is an unusual way to say she kissed the taste of herself off his mouth — the phrasing made me pause to work out what action was being described.
'he asked it into the warm disorder of her' — the 'it' is ambiguous and 'asked it into' is an oblique construction; I had to sit with it a beat to decide he was voicing his desire into her body.

'give that wanting air in daylight without making her pin it beneath a solemn name' — two abstract metaphors in succession. I understood the gist but had to unpack both images to be sure of the meaning.
The bridge metaphor is ungrounded — bridge between what and what? The sentence is philosophizing but the figure isn't anchored, so I had to work backward from the conclusion to guess the premise.

'in a register her mouth was still busy correcting' — the musical metaphor ('register') is clear enough, but the whole phrase packs a lot into a few words: her body said one thing, her mouth is still verbally walking it back. Took real effort to unpack on first read.

'the grammar she lived in' and 'that grammar walking' — the metaphor of social codes as grammar is extended here without preparation. I had to construct the mapping (grammar = the system of labels, lines, correct choices) while also reading the sentence forward.

'not the mirrors' — this term appears without prior establishment. I had to infer from context that 'mirrors' means women who reflect Randi back at herself, but the reference landed as a small puzzle.

The sentence structure is very hard to parse: multiple negations, an em-dash aside, a colon, and a fragment. 'Now, after — not before, not to be told what to want, but after the wanting had already shown' — I had to re-read to untangle the timing and negations, and then re-read again to connect the social animal clause to the question fragment.

'the geometry arranged across thirty feet arrived all at once' — reifying 'geometry' as something that can arrange and arrive is a noticeable poetic swerve; I had to translate it back to 'their converging paths met.'
